newsitem.title: USA: Fed adds reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed adds reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve added reserves to the banking system via a round of overnight system repurchase agreements on Monday, a New York Fed spokeswoman confirmed.
The 0938 EDT/1338 GMT operation came about an hour earlier than the Fed's usual intervention time.

Analysts said the Fed was forced to enter the open market early because quarter-end pressure and window dressing pushed up the Federal funds rate to 6.25 percent -- well above the 5.50 percent target.
Funds were also said tight due to the settlement of last week's two- and five-year notes.
The Fed's action was expected, given the Fed's hefty add need, projected at about $15 billion a day.
Monday's operation was deemed necessary since both Friday's coupon pass and seven-day fixed system RPs come off the books this session.
Still, operations of nine-day fixed and five-day fixed RPs remain on the books.
